We turned the microphone on our own product this week. WattPlan, the cycling training app we build at Manual Focus, now runs every line of its copy from one messaging house, and the proof column was written first, against the code. That caught five claims older documents still made and the product no longer supported. A workout count, a calendar export that was never built, two features listed as Premium that ship free. Each one was a sentence away from a store listing.

If you own a product's copy, the job to hand to AI is the proof column. Give it your feature documentation and every piece of live copy, and ask it to map each claim to a shipped feature. What comes back is the list of orphans, your corrections log on day one.

Older documents said more than a hundred workouts. The code has sixty-seven, so the house says "a structured library across every training zone". Calendar export was in a feature table, and there's no calendar writer in the code. Zwift export was listed as Premium, and it's free. So were Garmin and Wahoo workout push. And Ride Review had shipped on the second of September, so the house names the benefit, a Coach review after every ride. Every one of those was a sentence away from a store listing.

Our view at Manual Focus is that a messaging house earns its keep only when every claim traces to something the product does today, because a brand document you can't check against the product drifts from it within a release. We learned that on our own app, WattPlan, where writing the proof column first caught five stale claims before they reached a store listing.

Five steps. Proof column first. Retire lines in writing. Put the channel limits in the document. Route the benefits. Write the silence. The first is the job to hand to AI. Give it your feature documentation, or the codebase, and every piece of live copy, and ask it to map each claim to a shipped feature. Back comes a table of claims with the feature behind each, and a list of the orphans. That list is your corrections log on day one. The prompt is in the show notes.
